o: 6 a.m. on Tuesday
6 p.m. on Tuesday
6 p.m. on Monday
6 a.m. on Wednesday

questions.q:
A school's barometer log has readings taken on Monday at 8 a.m. and 9 p.m., on Wednesday at 2 p.m., on Thursday at 7 a.m. and on Saturday at 11 a.m.
(a) What fault in this log makes it weak for mapping and forecasting, according to the chapter?
(b) Write a reading schedule for a five-day week that removes the fault.
questions.a: (a) The readings were not taken at regular intervals; the chapter says readings taken at regular intervals help in mapping and forecasting. (b) For example: every day at 8 a.m. and 8 p.m., so that the gap between readings is the same each time.
s: Part (a): readings not at regular intervals
Part (b): a schedule with equal gaps, such as the same hours daily

questions.q:
Match each situation in Column I with the step in Column II that an accurate forecast or a suitable instrument makes possible.
Column I: 1. A cyclone is expected to reach a coastal district   2. Stormy weather is expected at sea   3. A glacial lake over 4800 metres up needs readings without anyone staying there   4. A school wants all its weather instruments together, read at regular intervals
Column II: (a) Fishermen are warned about venturing out in their boats   (b) A weather station is set up   (c) The entire coastal area may have to be evacuated   (d) An Automated Weather Station is installed
Choose the correct pairing.
questions.a: An expected cyclone may mean evacuating the coast (c); stormy weather at sea means warning fishermen (a); a remote lake needs a self-operating AWS (d); instruments brought together and read at regular intervals make a weather station (b). The other pairings swap two of these.

questions.q: A TV anchor says, 'Weather forecasts matter only to fishermen.' Which pair of examples from the chapter best answers her?
questions.a: Accurate predictions let local governments mobilise resources and prepare for disasters, and AWS data is used in fields like agriculture and aviation, so forecasts matter well beyond fishermen. The second pair is about fishermen and sailors, the third about traditional signs, and the fourth about instruments.
o: Governments mobilising resources for disasters, and AWS data used in agriculture and aviation
Fishermen being warned about venturing out in their boats, and sailors reading the wind data before a voyage
Elders reading ants and frogs for coming rain, and pine cones closing in humid conditions
A rain gauge placed in an open area, and a barometer reading displayed in millibars

questions.q: Meenal says, 'Weather predictions only warn us about storms and cyclones, so they are of no use in a district that has no coastline.' Is she right? Give reasons from the chapter.
questions.a: No. The chapter says climate change makes extreme weather such as droughts, floods and cyclones more frequent, and droughts and floods can occur inland. Accurate predictions help local governments mobilise resources and prepare for any disasters, and Automated Weather Station data is used in fields like agriculture and aviation, which need not be coastal.
s: Verdict: No
Droughts and floods are also extreme weather that forecasts help with
Governments prepare for any disasters; AWS data serves agriculture and aviation

questions.q: An Automated Weather Station records temperature, humidity, wind speed, wind direction, precipitation and atmospheric pressure once every hour. In one day it stores ___ values.

(a) Who set up the Automated Weather Station at a glacial lake in Sikkim, and in which year? (b) The lake lies more than 4800 metres above sea level. Using what the chapter says about high places, explain why a station that needs no person to read it suits the site.
questions.a: (a) The National Disaster Management Authority, in 2023. (b) At high altitude the air is thin and people feel breathless, dizzy or tired, so posting an observer is hard; an AWS works without human intervention and gives early information about upcoming weather.
s: Part (a): National Disaster Management Authority, 2023
Part (b): thin air makes staying hard; an AWS needs no person

questions.q:
Read the statements.
Statement 1: A weather station brings the instruments for several elements together, and its readings are taken at regular intervals, which helps in mapping and forecasting.
Statement 2: An Automated Weather Station can record wind speed, wind direction, humidity, precipitation, temperature and pressure without a person taking the readings.
Statement 3: Once an Automated Weather Station has recorded the data, the station itself carries out the scientific study that predicts the weather, so meteorologists are no longer needed.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: Statement 3 is false: meteorologists collect the data over long periods and study it with scientific methods to predict the weather. Statements 1 and 2 are in the chapter.
o: 1 and 2 only
1 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q: Compare an ordinary weather station and an Automated Weather Station under four headings: who takes the readings, where each can be placed, what each measures, and how the data are used. Then say which of the two suited the Sikkim glacial lake and why.
questions.a: In an ordinary weather station the instruments are brought together and readings are taken at regular intervals; in an AWS the sensors measure and record on their own. A staffed station needs people at the site, while an AWS can be placed where nobody can stay. Both measure the weather elements; the AWS measures and records temperature, humidity, wind speed and direction, precipitation and pressure. The data of both are used for mapping and forecasting, and the AWS data also serve agriculture, aviation, navigation and environmental monitoring. The Sikkim lake, more than 4800 m up, suited an AWS because it works without human intervention.
s: Readings: regular intervals by people against self-operating sensors
Placement: staffed site against remote places
What each measures: the elements, listed for the AWS
Use of the data: mapping and forecasting, and fields like agriculture and aviation
Sikkim lake suited an AWS because no person is needed

questions.q: A school's new weather corner has a thermometer, a rain gauge, a wind vane, an anemometer and a hygrometer, but no barometer. Which of these warnings could the corner not give from its own readings?
questions.a: A fall in pressure below 1000 mb, which indicates a depression, is read on a barometer, and the corner has none. Temperature, rainfall, wind speed and direction, and humidity are all covered by its other instruments.
o: That pressure has fallen below 1000 mb, showing a depression
That the day's maximum temperature has reached 42 degrees Celsius
That 60 mm of rain has fallen since early this morning
That the wind has risen to 45 km/h from the north

questions.q: A school says it has set up an Automated Weather Station by buying a thermometer and a rain gauge and asking a student to read them every day. Show why this does not match the chapter's Automated Weather Station.
questions.a: An Automated Weather Station is a self-operating system that uses sensors to measure and record the data without human intervention, but here a student reads the instruments by hand. It also measures five elements, including humidity, wind speed and direction, and atmospheric pressure, whereas the thermometer and rain gauge cover only temperature and precipitation.
s: The chapter's AWS is self-operating with sensors
A student reads by hand, so human intervention is needed
Only two of the five elements are covered

questions.q:
Assertion (A): An accurate forecast of a cyclone helps a local government prepare for it.
Reason (R): Climate change makes extreme weather such as droughts, floods and cyclones more frequent.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both are true. R is why forecasts matter more nowadays, but it does not explain how a forecast helps a government prepare (by letting it mobilise resources and warn people in advance), so it is not the explanation of A.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
The Assertion is true, but the Reason is false.
The Assertion is false, but the Reason is true.

questions.q:
A hill school wants a weather station on a ridge that, in the monsoon months, can be reached only by a three-hour climb. A manual station would need an observer paid 18,000 rupees a month, who would be unable to reach the ridge on about 10 days of each monsoon month. An Automated Weather Station would cost about 4.2 lakh rupees once. The school will run the project for 18 months, after which the town has promised to keep the station running for many years.
(a) What feature lets an Automated Weather Station keep recording on the days no observer can climb?
(b) What is the observer's total pay for 18 months, and is it more or less than the cost of the Automated Weather Station?
(c) After how many months does the observer's pay overtake the cost of the Automated Weather Station?
(d) Which station should the school choose? Decide and justify.
questions.a: (a) It is self-operating: its sensors measure and record the weather data without human intervention. (b) 18 x 18,000 = 3,24,000 rupees, which is 96,000 rupees less than 4,20,000. (c) 4,20,000/18,000 is about 23.3, so the observer's pay overtakes the cost during the 24th month. (d) The Automated Weather Station is supported: the town will run it for years, so it becomes the cheaper option after about 24 months, and it keeps recording in the monsoon months when the observer cannot reach the ridge. The observer is supported only if the answer accepts about 10 missing days in each monsoon month and weighs the 96,000 rupees saved over the 18 months of the project.
s: Part (a): self-operating sensors, no human intervention
Part (b): 3,24,000 rupees, less than 4.2 lakh
Part (c): during the 24th month
Part (d): decision weighing long-run cost and data gaps

questions.q:
Rajan says, 'The Automated Weather Station on the glacial lake forecasts the weather by itself, so no meteorologist is needed.'
(a) Say what the chapter says an Automated Weather Station does.
(b) Say who turns the long record into predictions, and how.
questions.a: (a) It is a self-operating system that uses sensors to measure and record weather data without human intervention. (b) Meteorologists, who collect the data over long periods, study it and use scientific methods to predict the weather.
s: Part (a): measures and records with sensors, self-operating
Part (b): meteorologists study the data with scientific methods to predict

questions.q: Stormy weather is expected at sea tonight. Write a two-line announcement for the fishermen of a coastal village. The first line gives the forecast; the second says what they must not do and who is making the arrangements for the coast.
questions.a: For example: 'Stormy weather is forecast at sea tonight. Do not take your boats out; the district administration is mobilising resources to protect the coast.' It states the forecast, tells fishermen not to venture out, and names the local authority preparing.
s: Line one states the forecast of stormy weather at sea
Line two tells them not to venture out and names the authority that prepares

questions.q: Two coastal towns each have a barometer. Town R reads it every hour and notes the figure. Town S reads it whenever a staff member remembers. A cyclone is expected within two days. Which statement is best supported by the chapter?
questions.a: Readings taken at regular intervals help in mapping and forecasting, so R's hourly log can reveal a dramatic fall in pressure. S's irregular readings do not give a trend. The 1000 mb mark is what indicates a depression, and the chapter does not limit forecasting to an AWS.
o: R's log can show how fast pressure is falling, since regular readings help forecasting
S's log is just as useful, since the barometer measures the same pressure whenever it is read
R's log is useful only if the pressure stays above 1000 mb throughout the two days
Neither log is of any use, since only an Automated Weather Station can help with forecasting

questions.q: Write one situation each in which data from an Automated Weather Station would be used by (i) a farmer, (ii) a ship's captain and (iii) a pilot, and name the element of weather each would rely on. Any sensible use of the five elements is accepted.
questions.a: For example: (i) a farmer uses precipitation data to decide when to irrigate; (ii) a ship's captain uses wind speed and direction before sailing; (iii) a pilot uses wind and pressure readings before take-off. Each situation is sensible and names an element from the five.
s: Farmer's situation with an element named
Ship captain's situation with an element named
Pilot's situation with an element named

questions.q: Climate change is making extreme weather more frequent. Argue why a country needs both Automated Weather Stations and meteorologists. Say what each contributes, why predictions matter more nowadays, and give two disasters with the action an accurate prediction allows.
questions.a: Automated Weather Stations use sensors to measure and record temperature, humidity, wind, precipitation and pressure without human intervention, even in remote places. Meteorologists collect such data over long periods and use scientific methods to predict how the weather will behave after hours, days or weeks. Predictions matter more nowadays because climate change makes droughts, floods and cyclones more frequent. For stormy weather at sea, fishermen can be warned not to venture out; for an expected cyclone, an entire coastal area might be evacuated, and local governments can mobilise resources for any disaster.
s: AWS contribution: sensors record without human intervention
Meteorologists study data over long periods and predict
Climate change makes extremes more frequent
A disaster with its action (fishermen warned)
A second disaster with its action (evacuation, mobilising resources)

questions.q:
A cyclone is forecast to reach the coast of an Odisha district in 36 hours. 40 fishing boats with 6 fishermen on each are in the harbour, and about 9,600 villagers may have to be moved to relief camps. Moving everyone takes about 20 hours. If the move is ordered now, about 1,800 working adults will lose two working days at 400 rupees a day each; the collector can instead wait 12 hours for a firmer forecast, which may show that the cyclone will pass by.
(a) Name two actions the chapter says an accurate forecast of stormy weather and of a cyclone allows.
(b) Which element is dominant while a cyclone is moving, and what barometer reading indicates a depression?
(c) Find the wage loss if the move is ordered now, and the time margin left if the collector waits 12 hours.
(d) Should the collector order the move now or wait 12 hours? Decide and justify.
questions.a: (a) Fishermen are warned about venturing out in their boats when stormy weather is expected at sea, and an entire coastal area might have to be evacuated if a cyclone is expected (local governments can also mobilise resources). (b) Atmospheric pressure; a reading below 1000 mb indicates a depression. (c) 1,800 x 2 x 400 = 14,40,000 rupees; waiting leaves 36 - 12 - 20 = 4 hours of margin. (d) Either choice earns the mark if it weighs the 14.4 lakh against a 4-hour margin on the lives of 9,600 people. Ordering now is supported because a margin of 4 hours is thin for a cyclone; waiting is supported if the answer starts warning the 240 fishermen at once and prepares transport so that the move can start the moment the forecast is firm.
s: Part (a): fishermen warned; evacuation or mobilising resources
Part (b): atmospheric pressure; below 1000 mb
Part (c): 14,40,000 rupees; 4 hours
Part (d): reasoned decision weighing the cost against the thin margin
